What if you drank only soda for thirty days?

Sugary drinks are one of the biggest sources of added sugar in the American diet. One can has about thirty nine grams of sugar, about ten teaspoons. Just three cans a day would be over ninety cans a month.

But here's the twist. That's more than the whole daily added sugar limit the American Heart Association suggests, in a single can, and the acid can wear down your tooth enamel! Even diet soda is still acidic, so plain water is the safest drink for your teeth.
